Our security engineering team needs to set up a proper isolated build pipeline for the SecPkg suite. We have three source packages in project/SRPMS/ (libcrypto-utils, auth-daemon, and secaudit) that must be built in completely isolated environments so they never contaminate each other or the host system.

Here's what we need:

1. Create a custom build environment configuration file (name it `secpkg-build.cfg`) tailored for our x86_64 Fedora 39 builds. It should define our build root identity, architecture constraints, package manager settings, and ensure the chroot has gcc, gcc-c++, make, and rpm-build pre-installed.

2. Use that configuration to build an SRPM from the spec file at project/SPECS/secpkg.spec (with its sources at project/SOURCES/). Store the result in results/single/. Make sure compiler caching is enabled to speed up future builds.

3. Write a shell script named `batch_build.sh` that rebuilds all three SRPMs from project/SRPMS/ using the same isolated configuration. Each package's build artifacts must land in its own subdirectory under results/batch/ so we can trace failures per-package. Then actually run that script.

We've tried doing this before with plain rpmbuild but it kept polluting our dev machines. The isolated chroot approach is mandatory.
